content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm facing an issue when writing to a VW entry of the [product_name]. I can read the value correctly, but when I try to write a 1 through my application, the [product_name] receives 1156 instead, and similar mismatches happen with other values. I'm not sure if I'm missing something in my setup. Any guidance would be appreciated.

More details are needed to analyze the difference between reading and writing. Try sending values such as 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 to see how the bits are shifting in the result. Please also specify which value you're writing to which address. It is recommended to use a free address range with a single VW address in the middle to avoid overlapping entries. Regards, [user_name]

Thank you for your response. I found that since the VM is represented only by WORD, reading displays a different number combination. Now, my question is about handling negative values: within the [product_name], these variables appear as negative, but in my C# program I'm unable to read them as such. Is there a method to correctly read negative numbers?

It depends on the declarations you use for the variables in C#. The values from [product_name] can be of different types based on the function. All analog values in arithmetic operations are signed integers (15 bits plus sign) stored in a word, for example VW0, VW2, VW4. Counter values are unsigned double integers (32 bits) stored in a dword, like VD100, VD104, VD108. Some specific functions use only 1 byte (8 bits) or BCD format (4 x 4 bits) in a word. Refer to the [document] or online help for detailed information about all functions and formats. [user_name]
